# Exercise video prompts

<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/generate-video-prompts.ts from src/data/exercises.ts — do not edit by hand. Re-run `npm run videos:prompts`. -->

Ready-to-paste prompts for AI-generated demonstration clips of all 95 exercises, all featuring the same athlete and set.
A CSV version (for spreadsheets or batch tools) is in `docs/exercise-video-prompts.csv`.

> **Review every clip before publishing.** AI video models regularly get exercise technique wrong — rounded backs, knees caving in,
> impossible joint angles, extra fingers, weights that pass through the body, or bars that bend. People will copy these videos with real
> load. Check each clip against its **Must show** and **Must NOT show** lists below, frame by frame if needed. If anything is off,
> regenerate it — never publish a clip you aren't sure about. A missing video is better than a wrong one.

## How to use this

1. **Keep the same athlete.** Generate one reference image first with the reference image prompt below. Pick the best result and
   reuse that exact image as the starting frame / character reference for every clip (image-to-video). Keep the same model, style
   settings and, if your tool supports it, the same seed. Don't change the outfit or the set between clips.
2. **Clip length:** 5–8 seconds. That's enough for 2–3 slow reps and loops nicely in the app.
3. **Aspect ratio:** 16:9 (1920×1080 or 1280×720) for the app. Optionally also render 9:16 (1080×1920) for social media.
4. **Format:** MP4 (H.264), no audio track needed, under 50 MB (the upload limit). WebM also works.
5. **File names:** save each clip as `<slug>.mp4` using the slug shown for each exercise (e.g. `back-squat.mp4`).
6. **Review** each clip with its checklist (see the warning above).
7. **Upload:** one at a time in Admin → Exercises → (exercise) → Demonstration media → Upload a file, or in bulk:

   ```bash
   npm run videos:import -- ./my-clips --license "AI-generated, owned by Narrow Gate Fitness" --attribution "Narrow Gate Fitness" --dry-run
   ```

   Remove `--dry-run` to actually upload. See SETUP.md → Exercise videos.

## Shared athlete & set

Every prompt below starts with this description so the athlete and set stay consistent:

```text
One consistent athlete: a fit, athletic adult with a natural, strong build, wearing a plain black fitted training top and black training shorts with subtle gold accents, black training shoes. Setting: a plain, uncluttered dark gym with a matte charcoal floor and walls, soft gold rim lighting from behind and to the side that outlines the body, even soft key light so the joints are clearly visible. Photorealistic, natural human proportions and anatomy, realistic weights and equipment.
```

## Exercises (95)

### 90/90 Hip Switch

- **File name:** `90-90-hip-switch.mp4`
- **Camera:** side view (shows the full range of motion)
- **Equipment:** Mat

**Prompt**

```text
One consistent athlete: a fit, athletic adult with a natural, strong build, wearing a plain black fitted training top and black training shorts with subtle gold accents, black training shoes. Setting: a plain, uncluttered dark gym with a matte charcoal floor and walls, soft gold rim lighting from behind and to the side that outlines the body, even soft key light so the joints are clearly visible. Photorealistic, natural human proportions and anatomy, realistic weights and equipment. Camera: locked-off on a tripod, side view (shows the full range of motion), full body and all equipment in frame, no camera movement, no cuts. Action: the athlete demonstrates the 90/90 Hip Switch (equipment: mat), already set up in the starting position. Movement: Sit with both knees bent at about 90 degrees, one leg in front and one to the side. Sit tall, using your hands behind you for support if needed. Rotate both knees to the other side so the legs switch positions. Continue switching slowly and with control. Perform 2–3 slow, controlled reps with a smooth full range of motion and a brief pause at the end range. Clearly visible form: sit tall; slow transitions; use hands if needed. End in the starting position so the clip loops cleanly. No text, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no music, no other people.
```

**Must show**

- [ ] Sit tall
- [ ] Slow transitions
- [ ] Use hands if needed
- [ ] Same athlete, outfit and set as the reference image; realistic anatomy and equipment

**Must NOT show**

- [ ] Slumping
- [ ] Forcing the knees down
- [ ] Moving quickly
- [ ] Distorted hands, limbs or equipment; weights passing through the body; text or logos

### Barbell Back Squat

- **File name:** `back-squat.mp4`
- **Camera:** 45° front-side view (shows depth, knee tracking and torso angle)
- **Equipment:** Barbell & plates, Squat rack

**Prompt**

```text
One consistent athlete: a fit, athletic adult with a natural, strong build, wearing a plain black fitted training top and black training shorts with subtle gold accents, black training shoes. Setting: a plain, uncluttered dark gym with a matte charcoal floor and walls, soft gold rim lighting from behind and to the side that outlines the body, even soft key light so the joints are clearly visible. Photorealistic, natural human proportions and anatomy, realistic weights and equipment. Camera: locked-off on a tripod, 45° front-side view (shows depth, knee tracking and torso angle), full body and all equipment in frame, no camera movement, no cuts. Action: the athlete demonstrates the Barbell Back Squat (equipment: barbell & plates, squat rack), already set up in the starting position. Movement: Set the bar in the rack at mid-chest height and step under it so it rests on your upper traps. Grip the bar just outside shoulder width, brace your core and unrack it with both feet. Take two or three steps back and set your feet about shoulder width, toes slightly turned out. Breathe in, brace, and sit down and back between your hips while keeping the bar over mid-foot. Descend to at least thighs parallel (or your controlled depth), then drive up through the whole foot to stand tall. Perform 2–3 slow, controlled reps with a smooth full range of motion and a brief pause at the end range. Clearly visible form: knees track over toes; chest proud, ribs down; push the floor away. End in the starting position so the clip loops cleanly. No text, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no music, no other people.
```

**Must show**

- [ ] Knees track over toes
- [ ] Chest proud, ribs down
- [ ] Push the floor away
- [ ] Same athlete, outfit and set as the reference image; realistic anatomy and equipment

**Must NOT show**

- [ ] Heels lifting off the floor
- [ ] Knees caving inward
- [ ] Losing the brace and rounding at the bottom
- [ ] Distorted hands, limbs or equipment; weights passing through the body; text or logos
